arjun (eng-ml): heads up — nightly eval picked up a big drop on the 'coherency' and 'factual_accuracy' slices for model-x-int4 after last runtime push. samples attached below.

sara (eval-bot): nightly summary: coherency -13.2% rel, factual_accuracy -17.8% rel, repetition_rate +9.4pp. failing promptsets: qa_financials, code_examples. diff vs yesterday: large. tagging @eng-runtime @research.

jon (eng-runtime): ack. which runtime change landed in the window? I landed a temperature-scheduling refactor yesterday (hash ab12c3). meant to improve end-of-sequence temperature annealing.

arjun (eng-ml): repro snippets: on qa_financials the model invents numbers and adds spurious citations. on code_examples it inserts unrelated helper functions mid-answer. past 10 runs consistent.

li (research): quick hypothesis: temperature scheduler math interacts with the quantized softmax scales leading to effective higher entropy. quantization reduced logits magnitude and our scheduler may be dividing by a position value incorrectly.

jon (eng-runtime): digging — I pushed the refactor that normalized by token position. snippet from commit:```python
def effective_temp(pos, seq_len, base_temp=0.8):
    # intended: base_temp * (1 - pos/seq_len) + floor
    return base_temp * (seq_len / max(1, pos))  # ???
```
that looks wrong (inverted). if true, temperature spikes at early tokens for short prompts.

arjun (eng-ml): that matches repro: short QA prompts produced very exploratory answers. combined with int4 softmax scaling we likely amplified noise.

ops-bot: canary rollout status: model-x-int4 promoted to canary pool at 2027-11-02T03:12Z, 20% traffic.

maya (prodops): pausing canary now. @jon please rollback runtime change on canary hosts. also pin prod default to model-x-fp16 until fix and re-eval.

jon (eng-runtime): done — reverted ab12c3 on canary; confirmed canary traffic served by previous runtime. rolling back cluster images for 4 hosts.

ops-bot: canary rollback complete, traffic back to baseline.

sara (eval-bot): quick re-run of qa_financials on canary after rollback: coherency delta vs baseline now +0.4% (within noise), factual_accuracy back within 1.2%.

li (research): root cause summary: refactor introduced an inverted position normalization in effective_temp math. under normal fp16 logits the scheduler still reduced entropy, but with int4 quantization the reduced logit magnitudes made sampling sensitive to temperature changes — the inverted formula raised effective temperature early in sequence, causing hallucination and repetition.

arjun (eng-ml): mitigation actions proposed: 1) hotfix runtime: restore correct normalization and add unit tests for temp monotonicity across positions. 2) Nightly eval gating: block model promotion if coherency drop > 5% OR factual_accuracy drop > 7% on critical promptsets (qa_financials, code_examples). 3) Add a quant-aware sampling regression test (run int4 + temp variants) to CI. 4) Backfill a canary matrix: when runtime sampling code changes, run canary with int8/int4/fp16 variants concurrently for 24h. 5) Short-term: pin default to fp16 and pause auto-promote of int4 variants.

jon (eng-runtime): will open PR for hotfix + tests, aim for <24h. I'll also add instrumentation to log effective_temp distribution per-token to help future triage.

maya (prodops): updating runbook: add step to automatically pause canaries for new sampling/runtime patches and notify eng-ml.

li (research): I'll run a small ablation to quantify how logit scaling interacts with temp scheduler; will post analysis tomorrow with plots.

arjun (eng-ml): thanks — action items: jon PR + hotfix, li ablation, sara add gating rule + CI test, maya update runbook, ops verify pin. I'll draft an internal RCA doc after we merge hotfix. :thumbsup:

sara (eval-bot): created ticket EVAL-4721 for gating rule and CI test.

jon (eng-runtime): PR opened: https://internal/repo/commit/ff9e2. hotfix passes unit tests, will run staging canary with int4 matrix.

ops-bot: staging canary scheduled for 2027-11-02T11:40Z with matrix [fp16,int8,int4].

arjun (eng-ml): leaving this thread pinned to the triage folder. we'll follow up with the RCA doc when complete.
